target_customer: Platforms and marketplaces in Latin America (ride hailing, delivery, payments) that want to offer working capital to their small business merchants and workers
problem: Small businesses in Latin America struggle to get credit, and platforms that hold their sales data lack the underwriting, compliance, servicing and capital markets stack to lend to them.
business_model: Embedded lending infrastructure, revenue-based financing funded by R2 and partner debt, earning loan interest and fees shared with platform partners

founders.name: Roger Larach
founders.background_notes: Launched Ualá's Mexico operations; earlier an M&A and restructuring investment banker focused on Latin America, per the YC page.

founders.name: Roger Teran
founders.background_notes: From El Salvador, started his career helping SMBs in Central America find growth capital, and angel invests in Latam founders, per the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed credit scoring from platform data, loan servicing, collections and integrations across countries. Standard fintech engineering, with the hard part being underwriting quality and funding sources rather than software.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integrations with platform partners, repayment and sales data and local lending know-how and funding lines were hard to replicate quickly, though lending models themselves are copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent absorbed the wedge. Platforms such as Uber, Rappi and PayU became partners, and Ant International invested in 2025.

market_need_then: SMB credit in Latin America was widely described as under-served, and platforms were looking for embedded finance offerings. Specific dated evidence from 2021 was not collected beyond the company's own framing.

branding.name_origin: A Bloomberg Linea Brazil article says the name is taken from a statistics concept; the specific concept was not stated in the snippet seen.

identity.logo: White R2 wordmark on the current site
identity.visual_style: Modern fintech marketing site with partner logos, country flags and line icons
identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and benefit focused, repeated calls to book a demo

brand_strength.rationale: A B2B infrastructure brand sold through partners whose own brands face the merchant. No sources show brand pull, and the short name is generic and shared with R2 object storage products.

outcome_analysis: R2 grew by embedding revenue-based loans inside large platforms such as Uber, Rappi and PayU, raising equity from General Catalyst and Gradient Ventures and a large debt facility to fund loans. It reports more than 200,000 SMBs financed. In October 2025 Ant International made a strategic investment, which the YC page describes as an acquisition, while press releases call it an investment.
notes: Directory status is Acquired and the YC page says acquired by Ant in 2025, but the October 2025 press release describes a strategic investment; terms and stake undisclosed. Bloomberg reported $59M in equity and debt in November 2024 per the YC page, only the $9M equity piece was verified separately. Competitor search found only 2022 and later sources (Fairplay, a55), so no dated competitors near the batch are listed.
